essential_question: How do I plan a season rather than a week?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe planning across a longer horizon with phases safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind planning across a longer horizon with phases and why it works.
Self-assess planning across a longer horizon with phases against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the planning across a longer horizon with phases task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: space and equipment appropriate to the chosen goal

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on planning across a longer horizon with phases.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind planning across a longer horizon with phases. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise planning across a longer horizon with phases with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies planning across a longer horizon with phases in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind planning across a longer horizon with phases and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies planning across a longer horizon with phases in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind planning across a longer horizon with phases and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of planning across a longer horizon with phases — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind planning across a longer horizon with phases before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of planning across a longer horizon with phases, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of planning across a longer horizon with phases; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking planning across a longer horizon with phases mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply planning across a longer horizon with phases under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, skill, coordination, or a functional task; any medical restriction is planned around with guardian input.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No body measurement, composition estimate, weight, or appearance target appears in the plan or its review. Phase success is defined by task performance.
inclusive_adaptation: Goals may be endurance, strength, mobility, skill, coordination, or a functional task; any medical restriction is planned around with guardian input.

guardian_safety.equipment: Depends on the chosen goal; bodyweight and free options are always viable.
guardian_safety.environment: Space appropriate to the goal.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Sustained progressive training. Guardian reviews the full cycle before it begins and at each review point.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian confirms the plan respects any medical restriction; the course asks only what movement is allowed.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting planning across a longer horizon with phases.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of planning across a longer horizon with phases in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What does real depth in one activity actually require?
learning_objectives: Sustain plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained sustained across a block long enough for the novelty to wear off, where practice has to continue without motivation, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal.
Explain what changed about plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained sustained across a block long enough for the novelty to wear off, where practice has to continue without motivation, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
materials: equipment for the chosen specialization or a substitute

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained sustained across a block long enough for the novelty to wear off, where practice has to continue without motivation.

Have the learner restate the critical features of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained sustained across a block long enough for the novelty to wear off, where practice has to continue without motivation. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained sustained across a block long enough for the novelty to wear off, where practice has to continue without motivation at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of plateau, boredom, and how depth is sustained yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Any activity the learner can access and perform is a valid specialization, including adapted sport, seated activity, and self-designed movement practice.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
Specialization is chosen by the learner, never assigned, and no activity is required that the household cannot access or afford.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. essential_question: What transfers between two very different activities, and what does not?
learning_objectives: Sustain managing two development goals without overloading run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal.
Explain what changed about managing two development goals without overloading under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own managing two development goals without overloading against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds managing two development goals without overloading run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
materials: equipment for the second activity or a substitute

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: managing two development goals without overloading run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery.

Have the learner restate the critical features of managing two development goals without overloading from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work managing two development goals without overloading run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works managing two development goals without overloading independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of managing two development goals without overloading and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works managing two development goals without overloading run alongside the first specialization, where the two goals compete for the same time and the same recovery at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of managing two development goals without overloading degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of managing two development goals without overloading — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind managing two development goals without overloading before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of managing two development goals without overloading, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of managing two development goals without overloading; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of managing two development goals without overloading for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking managing two development goals without overloading mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of managing two development goals without overloading yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Contrast may be in category, environment, pace, or social structure; a learner with limited access chooses two contrasting home-based activities.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.

essential_question: How do I make a movement better before I make it heavier or faster?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe programming strength and mobility into a wider plan safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan and why it works.
Self-assess programming strength and mobility into a wider plan against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the programming strength and mobility into a wider plan task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on programming strength and mobility into a wider plan.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise programming strength and mobility into a wider plan with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies programming strength and mobility into a wider plan in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies programming strength and mobility into a wider plan in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of programming strength and mobility into a wider plan — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind programming strength and mobility into a wider plan before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of programming strength and mobility into a wider plan, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of programming strength and mobility into a wider plan; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking programming strength and mobility into a wider plan mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. extension: Apply programming strength and mobility into a wider plan under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.

inclusive_adaptation: Every movement has a seated, supported, reduced-range, and unloaded version. Advancement criteria are set by control and range, never by load lifted relative to any other person.

guardian_safety.environment: Clear space with safe flooring.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Progressive loading and joint range work. Guardian reviews the progression and approves any external load before it is used.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian decides whether loaded work is supervised; the stop rule governs every session.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting programming strength and mobility into a wider plan.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. materials: equipment appropriate to the designed session

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: inclusive language, format, and scoring choices through a live session for safely available participants or a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through, evaluated against the same inclusion and enjoyment criteria.

Have the learner restate the critical features of inclusive language, format, and scoring choices from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work inclusive language, format, and scoring choices through a live session for safely available participants or a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through, evaluated against the same inclusion and enjoyment criteria. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of inclusive language, format, and scoring choices and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

Full transfer credit requires the session plan, access choices, feedback language, an in-session adaptation, and evaluation against the least-confident participant profile. formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of inclusive language, format, and scoring choices degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.

Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.

Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.

inclusive_adaptation: The session may be run for one person, for a household group, or delivered as a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through if no participants are available.

guardian_safety.movement_hazards: Depends on the session; the learner produces the safety plan and the guardian approves it before delivery.

Work self-assessment against LEVEL 2 expectations defended under questioning, including the part of the cycle that failed. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.
